measured_2026-07-30.note: Measured on the ai-eval scratch venv (onnxruntime + tokenizers installed, no torch). Confirms P1-A's lazy-loading requirement: AI modules import in milliseconds with zero model loading, and the real cost only lands on the first actual AI call, never at app/module import time.

interpretation: The ~2.5s CLIP first-use cost is real and disclosed, not hidden -- it is ONNX Runtime constructing an inference session from a 175.8MB fp16 model graph (the SHA256 integrity check itself is only ~260ms of that). It happens exactly once per process lifetime (module-level session cache), never at app startup, and never again until the process restarts. This is the intended trade-off: a brief one-time delay on the FIRST AI-analysis click, not a startup-blocking cost -- matching the spec's explicit 'lazy-load models on first AI use, never at startup' requirement.
old_torch_based_comparison: Not re-measured this session (would require reinstalling torch into a separate environment) -- the original torch-based code was ALREADY lazy-loaded on first use (module-level _model_cache, same pattern), so this change does not newly introduce lazy loading; it makes the lazily-loaded THING dramatically lighter (91.4MB torch-free ONNX session construction vs. constructing a torch nn.Module from a safetensors checkpoint plus torch's own import cost, which the old code's own docstring already characterized as 'the expensive part'). App/module import cost is unaffected by this change either way, since both old and new code deferred all heavy work behind first use.
